I've confirmed everything I need. Here is my review.

---

**DEFECT 1 — `src/misc/lv_text.c:653` — unconditional early return on NUL drops the offset advance that every iterator relies on, turning previously-terminating loops into infinite loops.**

```
if(txt == NULL || txt[*i] == '\0') return result;
```

The documented contract of `lv_text_utf8_next` (and the generic `lv_text_encoded_next` it backs) is "After call it will point to the next UTF-8 char". Previously, when `*i` pointed at the string's NUL terminator, `'\0'` was decoded as ASCII (`result = 0; (*i)++`), so the offset always advanced by at least one on every call. The new `txt[*i] == '\0'` branch returns without touching `*i`, so an offset parked on the NUL never moves.

`lv_text_encoded_next` / `lv_text_encoded_letter_next_2` are consumed inside `while(i < length)` loops whose termination depends entirely on `i` advancing — `lv_text_get_width` (`lv_text.c:399`), `lv_text_get_width_with_flags` (`lv_text.c:432`), and the `lv_label.c:595` loop. These accept a caller-supplied `length` (public API `lv_text_get_width`, legacy `lv_txt_get_width`). Concrete failure: `lv_text_get_width("abc", 10, font, 0)` — NUL is at index 3, so the loop runs `i=0,1,2,3`; at `i=3` the new branch returns 0 without advancing, `i` stays 3, and `while(3 < 10)` spins forever. Before this change the same call terminated (it returned a width). The added guard converts a previously-safe indefinite-bounded iteration into a hang for any `length` that extends past the string's NUL.

**DEFECT 2 — `src/misc/lv_text.c:653` (and the new tests) — the NULL/empty-string guard is UTF-8-only, so the exact NULL case the PR claims to fix (and its tests exercise) still crashes the binary built with `LV_TXT_ENC == LV_TXT_ENC_ASCII`.**

`lv_text_utf8_next` is compiled only under `#if LV_TXT_ENC == LV_TXT_ENC_UTF8` (`lv_text.c:544`); the ISO-8859-1 backend `lv_text_iso8859_1_next` (`lv_text.c:847`) is what `lv_text_encoded_next` points to under `LV_TXT_ENC_ASCII`, and it has no null check and does `uint8_t letter = txt[*i];` — a NULL dereference. Since `lv_text_encoded_letter_next_2` (`lv_text.c:538`) is encoding-agnostic and dereferences `txt[*ofs]`/`&txt[*ofs]`, the new `test_lv_text_encoded_letter_next_2_should_handle_null_pointer` (`tests/src/test_cases/test_txt.c:142`) and `..._should_handle_empty_string` tests, which carry no `LV_TXT_ENC` guard, pass only under the UTF-8 build and crash under an ASCII build. The claimed NULL-safety is silently backend-dependent; CI that only builds UTF-8 would never expose the crash. (On top of the inconsistency, the fix also behaves differently by backend: UTF-8 leaves `*ofs` at 0 for an empty/NULL input; ISO-8859-1 would have advanced it — so the two backends now disagree, unlike before.)

**DEFECT 1: Incomplete null-pointer fix — only UTF-8 decoder guarded, ISO-8859-1 decoder still dereferences NULL**

**File:** `src/misc/lv_text.c`  
**Line:** 847–854 (`lv_text_iso8859_1_next`)

The PR adds a null/empty-string guard to `lv_text_utf8_next` (line 652–653), but the same vulnerability exists in `lv_text_iso8859_1_next` which is used when `LV_TXT_ENC == LV_TXT_ENC_ASCII`:

```c
static uint32_t lv_text_iso8859_1_next(const char * txt, uint32_t * i)
{
    if(i == NULL) return txt[0];        // Line 849: dereferences NULL if txt == NULL
    uint8_t letter = txt[*i];           // Line 851: dereferences NULL if txt == NULL
    (*i)++;
    return letter;
}
```

**Failure scenario:**  
Build with `LV_TXT_ENC_ASCII`. Call `lv_text_encoded_letter_next_2(NULL, &letter, &letter_next, &ofs)` (or any caller that passes a NULL string to `lv_text_encoded_next`).  
→ `lv_text_iso8859_1_next` executes `txt[0]` or `txt[*i]` on a NULL pointer → **segmentation fault**.

The fix must be applied to both encoding variants, or the guard must be moved to the shared caller `lv_text_encoded_letter_next_2` (which currently has no null check itself).
